findings.problem: M4-77-AC-08 requires generation-1 observation/finalization to use fresh post-lock PostgreSQL time. TC-10 proves expired-owner fencing and zero PostgreSQL writes, but its executable procedure does not create a discriminating observation/finalization clock test: it does not start observation/finalization before lease expiry, block that operation on the relevant PostgreSQL lock until after expiry, compare transaction-start/application time against a fresh post-lock clock_timestamp(), and capture the deciding database-time sample. The expected result only states that expired operations use fresh post-lock PostgreSQL time, while the evidence list contains execution snapshots, observation/audit identities, row-set digest and write traces but no post-lock database-time evidence. A materially nonconforming implementation using transaction-start or application time for observation/finalization can therefore satisfy the stated fencing/zero-write observations in the tested scheduling arrangement. The separate TC-04 clock test applies to acquisition/admission expiry and does not prove the distinct observation/finalization requirement.
findings.required_change: Extend TC-10 with discriminating observation and finalization races on both sides of the generation-1 lease boundary. For each operation, begin before expiry, hold it behind the governing PostgreSQL lock, cross expiry while blocked, skew non-database/application clocks, then release the lock and require the decision to use a captured post-lock clock_timestamp() that is later than the lease deadline. Add a before-expiry control proving the same path is not spuriously fenced. Evidence must record the lease deadline, transaction/application clock values, fresh post-lock PostgreSQL time, lock ordering and resulting state/write counts for observation and finalization independently.

findings.problem: The v4 denial table closes the ProposalNotExecutable result type, lifecycle, outcome_type, reason_code, HTTP status, HTTP key set and public error code, but it does not independently close the values or value domains of proposal_id and logical_execution_id. The execution-outcome table explicitly requires both IDs to be canonical lowercase RFC 4122 UUIDs read from durable proposal/execution identity, whereas the denial section only says those two fields are present. TC-03 and TC-10 then require comparison with an independently loaded exact row and complete field/value domains without specifying an independent source or equality oracle for the two denial identities. Consequently a denial mapper that substitutes the wrong proposal or logical-execution identity can satisfy the written denial-row oracle if the fixture checks only shape/static values or derives the identity from the produced projection. This leaves M4-77-GR-007 incompletely closed because its required exact ProposalNotExecutable application projection is not fully independently specified.
findings.required_change: Close proposal_id and logical_execution_id in the denial matrix itself: define their canonical value domain and require exact equality to independently seeded/reloaded durable proposal and acquisition logical-execution identities for every denial scenario. State that the independent TC-03/TC-10 fixture obtains those expected identities from scenario authority established before invoking the application/HTTP seam and must never copy or derive them from the returned ProposalNotExecutable projection or production mapper. Capture expected-versus-actual identity values per row in release evidence. Apply this oracle in both TC-03 and TC-10.

summary: Guide v4 substantially preserves the approved generation-1, static-registry and no-#78-recovery boundaries and retains strong acquisition, admission, provider-atomicity, fencing, audit, DI-isolation and regression evidence. It cannot be approved yet because TC-10 does not contain an executable oracle proving fresh post-lock PostgreSQL time specifically for observation/finalization, and the new post-acquisition denial matrix does not independently close the two dynamic identity values in every ProposalNotExecutable application projection. Therefore M4-77-AC-08 and M4-77-AC-09 are not yet adequately proven, and M4-77-GR-007 is not fully closed.
